# Paste-ready fixes: iOS

These snippets are released under MIT-0: use them in any app, no attribution needed. Adapt names to the project, keep the logic.

## IOS-001: App Transport Security is turned off

Remove NSAllowsArbitraryLoads and NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent from Info.plist (and any INFOPLIST_KEY_ build setting that adds them). If one host really needs HTTP, add a narrow NSExceptionDomains entry for that host only.

```xml
<key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
<dict>
    <!-- No NSAllowsArbitraryLoads: ATS blocks plain HTTP and requires TLS 1.2+. -->
    <!-- Only if one host truly needs HTTP: -->
    <!--
    <key>NSExceptionDomains</key>
    <dict>
        <key>legacy.example.com</key>
        <dict>
            <key>NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads</key>
            <true/>
        </dict>
    </dict>
    -->
</dict>
```

Verify: Build the release configuration, open an http:// URL your app uses, and confirm the request fails with an App Transport Security error.

Book: [§7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

## IOS-003: A TLS version below 1.2 is allowed

Delete the NSExceptionMinimumTLSVersion entry (ATS then enforces TLS 1.2), and set tlsMinimumSupportedProtocolVersion to .TLSv12 or higher in code.

```swift
// URLSession. ATS already enforces 1.2; raise it only if every server you call speaks 1.3.
let configuration = URLSessionConfiguration.default
configuration.tlsMinimumSupportedProtocolVersion = .TLSv12
```

Verify: Point a test build at a server limited to TLS 1.1 (for example `openssl s_server -accept 8443 -tls1_1 -cipher 'DEFAULT:@SECLEVEL=0' -cert cert.pem -key key.pem` behind a test hostname) and confirm the app refuses the connection.

Book: [§7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

## IOS-004: A server-trust handler accepts certificates without validating them

Validate the chain with SecTrustEvaluateWithError before anything else, cancel the challenge when it fails, and only then compare pins. If you don't pin, return .performDefaultHandling.

```swift
// Or delete this delegate method entirely: the default handling validates for you.
// Pinning: see IOS-005 and IOS-007 (high-risk apps only).
func urlSession(
    _ session: URLSession,
    didReceive challenge: URLAuthenticationChallenge
) async -> (URLSession.AuthChallengeDisposition, URLCredential?) {

    guard challenge.protectionSpace.authenticationMethod == NSURLAuthenticationMethodServerTrust,
          let trust = challenge.protectionSpace.serverTrust else {
        return (.performDefaultHandling, nil)
    }

    // Validate the chain the normal way: trusted root, dates, hostname.
    let policy = SecPolicyCreateSSL(true, challenge.protectionSpace.host as CFString)
    SecTrustSetPolicies(trust, policy)
    guard SecTrustEvaluateWithError(trust, nil) else {
        return (.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
    }
    return (.useCredential, URLCredential(trust: trust))
}
```

Verify: Route the app through a proxy whose CA the device does not trust (mitmproxy, §22.3) and confirm every request fails with a TLS error.

Book: [§8.10](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#810-how-to-implement-it)

## IOS-005: Pinning code falls back to default handling when no pin matches

Return .cancelAuthenticationChallenge when the chain fails validation and when no pin matches. Use .performDefaultHandling only for challenges that aren't server trust.

```swift
func urlSession(
    _ session: URLSession,
    didReceive challenge: URLAuthenticationChallenge
) async -> (URLSession.AuthChallengeDisposition, URLCredential?) {

    guard challenge.protectionSpace.authenticationMethod == NSURLAuthenticationMethodServerTrust,
          let trust = challenge.protectionSpace.serverTrust else {
        return (.performDefaultHandling, nil)
    }

    // 1. Validate the chain the normal way first: trusted root, dates, hostname.
    let policy = SecPolicyCreateSSL(true, challenge.protectionSpace.host as CFString)
    SecTrustSetPolicies(trust, policy)
    guard SecTrustEvaluateWithError(trust, nil) else {
        return (.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
    }

    // 2. Only then compare pins, across the whole evaluated chain (SPKIPin: book §8.10).
    let chain = (SecTrustCopyCertificateChain(trust) as? [SecCertificate]) ?? []
    if chain.contains(where: { SPKIPin.of($0).map(pins.contains) == true }) {
        return (.useCredential, URLCredential(trust: trust))
    }

    // 3. No pin matched. Refuse. Never fall back to .performDefaultHandling here.
    return (.cancelAuthenticationChallenge, nil)
}
```

Verify: Make the pin set wrong in a test build and confirm requests fail with NSURLErrorCancelled (-999), as in §8.10.

Book: [§8.10](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#810-how-to-implement-it)

## IOS-006: Pinned domain has no backup pin

Add a second SPKI-SHA256-BASE64 entry: a backup key at a second CA, or a key you hold offline. If you list both CA and leaf identities, each list needs its own backup.

```xml
<key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
<dict>
    <key>NSPinnedDomains</key>
    <dict>
        <key>api.example.com</key>
        <dict>
            <key>NSIncludesSubdomains</key>
            <true/>
            <!-- Pins an intermediate or root. Use NSPinnedLeafIdentities to pin the leaf. -->
            <key>NSPinnedCAIdentities</key>
            <array>
                <dict>
                    <key>SPKI-SHA256-BASE64</key>
                    <string>YLh1dUR9y6Kja30RrAn7JKnbQG/uEtLMkBgFF2Fuihg=</string>
                </dict>
                <dict>
                    <!-- Backup pin -->
                    <key>SPKI-SHA256-BASE64</key>
                    <string>Vjs8r4z+80wjNcr1YKepWQboSIRi63WsWXhIMN+eWys=</string>
                </dict>
            </array>
        </dict>
    </dict>
</dict>
```

Verify: Serve a test endpoint with a certificate issued for the backup key (or from the backup CA) and confirm the app connects. Then confirm that a certificate matching neither pin fails.

Book: [§8.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#86-where-the-pins-live-static-dynamic-and-hybrid)

## IOS-007: No certificate pinning (needed for high-risk apps)

Pin the SPKI of your intermediate CA with NSPinnedDomains (simplest) or a URLSessionDelegate that validates first, plus a backup pin and a written rotation runbook. Pin only if you can also run failure alerts, CT monitoring, and a protected kill switch (§8.7); if not, don't pin and rely on strict TLS plus CT (§8.9).

```xml
<key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
<dict>
    <key>NSPinnedDomains</key>
    <dict>
        <key>api.example.com</key>
        <dict>
            <key>NSIncludesSubdomains</key>
            <true/>
            <!-- Pins an intermediate or root. Use NSPinnedLeafIdentities to pin the leaf. -->
            <key>NSPinnedCAIdentities</key>
            <array>
                <dict>
                    <key>SPKI-SHA256-BASE64</key>
                    <string>YLh1dUR9y6Kja30RrAn7JKnbQG/uEtLMkBgFF2Fuihg=</string>
                </dict>
                <dict>
                    <!-- Backup pin -->
                    <key>SPKI-SHA256-BASE64</key>
                    <string>Vjs8r4z+80wjNcr1YKepWQboSIRi63WsWXhIMN+eWys=</string>
                </dict>
            </array>
        </dict>
    </dict>
</dict>
```

Verify: Make the device trust a proxy CA, then confirm requests to pinned hosts fail while an unpinned host still loads through the proxy (§8.10, step 1).

Book: [§8.8](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#88-the-decision-by-application-type)

## IOS-008: Keychain item is readable before the first unlock

Use kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly. If background work needs the item while the phone is locked, use kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly.

```swift
let attributes: [String: Any] = [
    kSecValueData as String: token,
    // WhenUnlocked: needs an unlocked device. ThisDeviceOnly: never migrates
    // to another device. See §4.4.
    kSecAttrAccessible as String: kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly,
]
// Background refresh while locked? Use kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly,
// never kSecAttrAccessibleAlways.
```

Verify: Search the code for kSecAttrAccessibleAlways and confirm no match. On a test device, lock it and confirm background code that needs the item behaves as you expect.

Book: [§4.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#44-data-protection-classes-the-decision-you-keep-getting-wrong)

## IOS-009: Keychain item can migrate to another device

Append ThisDeviceOnly: kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly, or AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly for items that background work needs. Skip this for items you sync on purpose with kSecAttrSynchronizable.

```swift
let attributes: [String: Any] = [
    kSecValueData as String: token,
    // WhenUnlocked: needs an unlocked device. ThisDeviceOnly: never migrates
    // to another device. See §4.4.
    kSecAttrAccessible as String: kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly,
]
// Background refresh while locked? Use kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly,
// never kSecAttrAccessibleAlways.
```

Verify: Back up a test device, restore it onto a second device, and confirm the app asks the user to sign in again.

Book: [§4.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#44-data-protection-classes-the-decision-you-keep-getting-wrong)

## IOS-010: File written with no Data Protection

Write sensitive files with .completeFileProtection, and exclude them from backup. Use completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication only for files background work must read while locked.

```swift
func writeSensitive(_ data: Data, to url: URL) throws {
    try data.write(to: url, options: [.atomic, .completeFileProtection])
    var values = URLResourceValues()
    values.isExcludedFromBackup = true
    var fileURL = url
    try fileURL.setResourceValues(values)
}
```

Verify: On a physical device, write the file, lock the phone, and confirm code that runs while locked can't read it (the simulator doesn't enforce Data Protection).

Book: [§4.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#44-data-protection-classes-the-decision-you-keep-getting-wrong)

## IOS-011: Token or password stored in UserDefaults

Keep short-lived tokens in memory. Store long-lived tokens and credentials in the Keychain with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly. Leave only non-secret settings in UserDefaults.

```swift
func storeToken(_ token: Data, account: String,
                service: String = "com.example.app.session") throws {
    let query: [String: Any] = [
        kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword,
        kSecAttrService as String: service,
        kSecAttrAccount as String: account,
    ]
    let attributes: [String: Any] = [
        kSecValueData as String: token,
        kSecAttrAccessible as String: kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly,
    ]

    // Update in place if it exists; add it if not. No delete-then-add window.
    var status = SecItemUpdate(query as CFDictionary, attributes as CFDictionary)
    if status == errSecItemNotFound {
        let newItem = query.merging(attributes) { _, new in new }
        status = SecItemAdd(newItem as CFDictionary, nil)
    }
    guard status == errSecSuccess else { throw KeychainError.unexpectedStatus(status) }
}
```

Verify: On the simulator, sign in, then run `grep -rl "eyJ" "$(xcrun simctl get_app_container booted <bundle id> data)/Library/Preferences"` and confirm there is no output. UserDefaults is a binary plist, so don't add `-I`. If your tokens aren't JWTs, search for a known part of one instead.

Book: [§6.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#64-the-uncomfortable-question-nobody-asked)

## IOS-012: Biometric check only flips a boolean

Bind the prompt to a key: create a Secure Enclave key with SecAccessControl [.privateKeyUsage, .biometryCurrentSet] and sign a server challenge with it. The server accepts the action only with a valid signature.

```swift
// Create the key with [.privateKeyUsage, .biometryCurrentSet] (book §6.6), register its
// public key with your server, then sign the server's challenge. The Face ID / Touch ID sheet
// appears as part of using the key: there is no boolean to hook.
let context = LAContext()
context.localizedReason = reason
let query: [String: Any] = [
    kSecClass as String: kSecClassKey,
    kSecAttrApplicationTag as String: tag,
    kSecAttrKeyType as String: kSecAttrKeyTypeECSECPrimeRandom,
    kSecReturnRef as String: true,
    kSecUseAuthenticationContext as String: context
]
var item: CFTypeRef?
let status = SecItemCopyMatching(query as CFDictionary, &item)
guard status == errSecSuccess, let item else { throw BiometricKeyError.keyMissing(status) }
let privateKey = item as! SecKey

var error: Unmanaged<CFError>?
guard let signature = SecKeyCreateSignature(
    privateKey, .ecdsaSignatureMessageX962SHA256, message as CFData, &error
) as Data? else {
    throw BiometricKeyError.signingFailed(error?.takeRetainedValue())
}
// Send `signature` with the request; the server verifies it with the enrolled public key.
```

Verify: Hook evaluatePolicy to report success (for example, `ios ui biometrics_bypass` in objection) and confirm the protected action still fails because no valid signature reaches the server.

Book: [§11.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#111-decorative-versus-real)

## IOS-013: Biometric key stays valid after a new fingerprint or face is enrolled

Replace .biometryAny with .biometryCurrentSet, and handle the signing failure that follows an enrollment change by sending the user to re-enroll or to server-side step-up.

```swift
guard let access = SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags(
    kCFAllocatorDefault,
    kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly,   // unusable if the passcode is removed
    [.privateKeyUsage, .biometryCurrentSet],           // "CurrentSet", not "Any": §11.3
    &cfError
) else { throw cfError!.takeRetainedValue() as Error }
```

Verify: Add a new fingerprint or re-enroll Face ID on a test device, use the feature again, and confirm signing fails and the app asks the user to re-enroll.

Book: [§11.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#113-the-enrollment-problem-nobody-thinks-about)

## IOS-014: Web view inspection is on in release builds

Wrap the line in #if DEBUG so it never compiles into release builds.

```swift
let webView = WKWebView(frame: .zero, configuration: config)
#if DEBUG
if #available(iOS 16.4, *) { webView.isInspectable = true }   // never in release
#endif
```

Verify: Install the release build on a device connected to a Mac, open a web view screen, and confirm your app doesn't appear in Safari's Develop menu.

Book: [§16.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#166-cleanup-and-hygiene)

## IOS-015: Script message handler doesn't check who sent the message

In the handler, reject messages unless frameInfo.isMainFrame is true and frameInfo.securityOrigin is your https host. Then validate every argument, and let the server authorize the action.

```swift
func userContentController(_ userContentController: WKUserContentController,
                           didReceive message: WKScriptMessage) async -> (Any?, String?) {
    // 1. Who is calling? WebKit has no origin allowlist for handlers, so check here.
    let origin = message.frameInfo.securityOrigin
    guard message.frameInfo.isMainFrame,
          origin.protocol == "https",
          origin.host == "app.example.com" else { return (nil, "rejected") }

    // 2. What did they send? Untrusted input.
    guard let code = message.body as? String,
          code.range(of: #"^[A-Z0-9]{8}$"#, options: .regularExpression) != nil
    else { return (nil, "invalid") }

    // 3. The server authorizes. The bridge only relays.
    do {
        try await redeem(code)
        return ("received", nil)
    } catch {
        return (nil, "failed")
    }
}
```

Verify: Load a page from a different origin in the same web view, post a message to each handler name, and confirm every handler rejects it.

Book: [§16.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#162-the-javascript-bridge-and-why-its-the-sharpest-edge)

## IOS-017: Sign-in callback uses a custom URL scheme

Return to a verified https redirect: Universal Links (Associated Domains applinks:) and, on iOS 17.4+, ASWebAuthenticationSession with .https(host:path:). Keep PKCE and state either way.

```swift
// In a class with `private var session: ASWebAuthenticationSession?`
let session = ASWebAuthenticationSession(
    url: authorizeURL,   // carries code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256 and state
    callback: .https(host: "auth.example.com", path: "/oauth/callback") // iOS 17.4+
) { callbackURL, error in
    guard let callbackURL, error == nil else { return } // canceled or failed
    // Check `state`, then send `code` plus the verifier to the token endpoint.
    _ = callbackURL
}
session.presentationContextProvider = self
self.session = session   // keep a strong reference until the callback runs
session.start()
```

Verify: Install a test app that registers the same scheme, start sign-in, and confirm the callback can't reach it once the https redirect is in place.

Book: [§17.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#175-deep-links-and-the-verification-that-makes-them-safe)

## IOS-018: Insecure NSKeyedUnarchiver API

Decode with Codable. If you must read NSKeyedArchiver data, use unarchivedObject(ofClass:from:) with an NSSecureCoding class.

```swift
// Best for new code: Codable builds only the types you declared.
let order = try JSONDecoder().decode(Order.self, from: data)

// If you must read NSKeyedArchiver data: secure coding with an explicit class.
let legacyOrder = try NSKeyedUnarchiver.unarchivedObject(ofClass: LegacyOrder.self, from: data)
```

Verify: Search the code for unarchiveObject(with and unarchiveTopLevelObjectWithData and confirm no match remains.

Book: [§19.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#194-deserialization)

## IOS-019: App target has no privacy manifest

Add a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy to the app target (File > New > File > App Privacy) and fill in what the app and its SDKs collect and why.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>NSPrivacyTracking</key>
    <false/>
    <key>NSPrivacyTrackingDomains</key>
    <array/>
    <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes</key>
    <array/>
    <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes</key>
    <array>
        <dict>
            <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType</key>
            <string>NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults</string>
            <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons</key>
            <array><string>CA92.1</string></array>
        </dict>
    </array>
</dict>
</plist>
```

Verify: Archive the app, then in Xcode's Organizer choose Generate Privacy Report and confirm it lists your app's manifest.

Book: [§18.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#183-transparency-and-control)

## IOS-020: Secret copied to the general pasteboard without localOnly

Copy secrets only when the user asks, with setItems(_:options:) and the options .localOnly: true and an .expirationDate.

```swift
import UniformTypeIdentifiers

UIPasteboard.general.setItems(
    [[UTType.plainText.identifier: sensitiveValue]],
    options: [
        .localOnly: true,                                // do not sync to other devices
        .expirationDate: Date().addingTimeInterval(60)   // clears itself
    ]
)
```

Verify: Copy the value in the app, then try pasting on a second device signed in to the same Apple Account, and confirm nothing arrives; wait past the expiration and confirm the pasteboard is empty.

Book: [§6.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#66-how-to-implement-it)

## IOS-021: Release build keeps symbols or testability

In the Release configuration set ENABLE_TESTABILITY = NO and STRIP_INSTALLED_PRODUCT = YES, and keep symbols in a separate dSYM (DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT = dwarf-with-dsym) for crash reports.

```xcconfig
// Release.xcconfig
DEPLOYMENT_POSTPROCESSING = YES
STRIP_INSTALLED_PRODUCT = YES
STRIP_STYLE = all
STRIP_SWIFT_SYMBOLS = YES
DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT = dwarf-with-dsym
ENABLE_TESTABILITY = NO
```

Verify: Archive the release build and run `nm -U` on the app binary: you should see few or no readable Swift or Objective-C symbol names.

Book: [§15.8](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#158-build-configuration-in-code)
